title: WhatsApp Rolls Out Third-Party AI Agent Chats on Android Beta
excerpt: Users can now connect up to five external AI agents or bots to their WhatsApp account, each running in an isolated conversation — but without end-to-end encryption.
body:
• WhatsApp is testing a feature that lets users connect third-party AI agents and bots directly within the app via a new Agents section in settings
  • Each agent gets its own dedicated chat and can only see messages shared in that conversation — no access to other chats, contacts, or media
  • Agent conversations are not end-to-end encrypted because messages are processed through a Meta-managed service on behalf of the developer
  • The rollout comes shortly after the European Commission ordered Meta to restore free API access for rival AI assistants on WhatsApp

WhatsApp has begun rolling out a feature that allows users to connect third-party AI agents and bots directly within the messaging app, according to WABetaInfo, which discovered the functionality in the WhatsApp beta for Android version 2.26.35.3.

The feature is currently available to a limited number of users in select countries, with no announced timeline for a broader release. But the move signals WhatsApp's ambition to become a platform for AI services beyond Meta's own assistant.

How the Feature Works

Users can set up agents through a new Agents section in WhatsApp's settings. The process involves naming the agent, choosing a profile picture, and generating an API key. That key is then entered on whatever platform hosts the agent — OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, or any compatible service — to establish the connection.

Once linked, the agent appears as a separate conversation in the user's chat list. WhatsApp supports up to five agents per account, allowing users to connect different assistants for different purposes — a scheduling bot, a customer support agent, or a general AI assistant.

The feature is not limited to AI-powered services. Any compatible bot or automated service can be connected using the generated API key.

Privacy Architecture: Isolated but Not Encrypted

WhatsApp has built privacy protections into the feature's design. Each agent operates in a sandboxed conversation and can only read messages the user sends directly to it. The agent has no access to other WhatsApp chats, contacts, or media stored on the device.

However, conversations with agents are explicitly not end-to-end encrypted. WhatsApp explains that because a Meta-operated service sits between the user and the agent developer to facilitate the connection, the standard encryption that protects personal messages does not apply. The agent developer can access messages as part of the service.

"WhatsApp considers messages end-to-end encrypted only when they go directly between the devices of the people in the conversation. Since chats with agents are managed by a Meta service on behalf of the agent developer, they are not considered end-to-end encrypted."

— WABetaInfo

Regular personal messages and calls between WhatsApp users remain fully end-to-end encrypted and are unaffected by this feature.

Managing and Removing Agents

Users can rename agents, change their profile pictures, and regenerate API keys at any time. Removing an agent disconnects it from the chat, but WhatsApp preserves the conversation history — users can still read past messages. Reconnecting requires creating the agent again with a new API key.

For now, agents can only operate in individual chats. They cannot be added to group conversations or communities.

Regulatory Context

The timing of WhatsApp's third-party agent support is notable. The rollout comes shortly after the European Commission ordered Meta to restore free access to the WhatsApp Business API for rival general-purpose AI assistants. Meta had originally blocked competing AI bots in October 2025, then briefly allowed them back under a paid arrangement that regulators deemed equivalent to a ban.

Meta is appealing the Commission's order, but it remains in force until the EU's wider antitrust investigation concludes or June 2029, whichever comes first. The third-party agent feature represents a different approach — letting users themselves connect external services rather than having those services operate through the WhatsApp Business API.

What It Means for India's 500 Million WhatsApp Users

India is WhatsApp's largest market by user count, and the platform is deeply integrated into daily life — from family group chats to small business communications and government services. The ability to connect external AI agents could transform how millions of users interact with customer support, banking services, and healthcare bots without leaving the app they already use for everything.

For Indian small businesses already using WhatsApp Business, the feature could offer a path to AI-powered customer service without the cost of enterprise solutions. Whether the trade-off on encryption will concern Indian users — who have historically prioritized convenience over privacy on messaging platforms — remains to be seen.
nri_angle: India is WhatsApp's largest market with over 500 million users; the ability to connect third-party AI agents directly within WhatsApp could reshape how Indian businesses and consumers interact with AI-powered services.
